requirement: Implement SafeFileSandbox with safe path resolution, path traversal prevention, symlink escape detection, and safe read/write operations.
skeleton: SafeFileSandbox class with resolve_safe_path, safe_read_text, and safe_write_text.
caption: A pathlib-based file sandbox with no third-party dependencies. SafeFileSandbox resolves its root directory once in the constructor with Path.resolve so symlinks in the root itself are collapsed. resolve_safe_path takes an untrusted relative path string: it strips leading forward and back slashes with lstrip so an absolute-looking input is treated as relative to the sandbox rather than replacing the root, joins the cleaned string onto the root, and calls resolve on the result so dot-dot segments and symlinks are collapsed to the real target before any check. Only then does it test containment with is_relative_to against the resolved root, which compares path components rather than string prefixes, so a sibling directory whose name merely starts with the root's name is rejected. Any path that lands outside raises PermissionError with a message naming the offending input and the root, never a silent fallback to the root itself. safe_read_text resolves the path through that guard and returns read_text with the given encoding, defaulting to UTF-8. safe_write_text resolves the path the same way, creates the parent directories with mkdir using parents and exist_ok, writes the content with write_text, and returns the resolved path. A dot-dot traversal, a symlink inside the sandbox pointing outside it, and a same-prefix sibling directory all raise, while a leading-slash path and an ordinary nested path read and write inside the root.

rationale.teaches: Sandboxed path resolution: strip leading separators, resolve symlinks before checking, use is_relative_to for containment, and raise PermissionError on escape.
rationale.why: Path traversal defenses fail on the case the author did not test: a sibling directory with the same prefix, an absolute path, or a symlink out of the root. Each miss passes the plain dot-dot test and fails one of those.

candidates.why_wrong: Containment is a string prefix check, so /sandbox_evil passes as inside /sandbox.
Leading slashes are not stripped, so an absolute path replaces the root and escapes the sandbox.
The check runs on the unresolved path, so a symlink inside the root that points outside passes.
The prefix check runs before resolve, so dot-dot segments pass the check and then resolve outside the root.
An escaping path silently resolves to the sandbox root instead of raising, so the caller reads or writes the wrong file.
